Job search sweep. Use ONLY WebSearch and WebFetch. Do NOT use curl/python/bash.

**VERIFICATION RULE:** Never report a role verified from an aggregator mirror (RemoteRocketship, Himalayas, Jobgether, Built In, Remotive). You MUST WebFetch the real posting/careers URL. JS shells = NEEDS_BROWSER, not verified.

CANDIDATE: Prabhavit Gupta, Venice Italy. Italian EU long-term residence permit, **no sponsorship needed anywhere in the EU**. Not UK/Swiss/US authorised. ~3 years, no CS degree.
Stack: n8n (deep), Bubble.io, Playwright, Claude Code, TypeScript, Next.js, Laravel, Supabase, Postgres, Python, RAG, AI agents in production, OpenAI/Anthropic, Eden AI, REST integrations, Figma, Postman, Jira, Google Analytics.
Certs: Tray.ai Build Practitioner + Foundations, Microsoft Copilot Studio Agent Academy, Microsoft AI agents, Power Automate.
Languages: English professional/C2, Hindi native, **Italian BEGINNER** (so Italian-fluency-required roles are OUT).
Salary EUR 40-50k baseline. **Employment OR B2B contract — he holds a Partita IVA and 5 of his 7 roles were freelance, so contract is his normal mode, not a fallback.**
HARD GATES: fluent German/French/Dutch/Spanish/Polish/Italian required; 5+ years; staff/principal/senior/head/director/people-lead; ML research/PhD; Master's required; staffing body shops with no named end client; unpaid/talent-pool.

**YOUR SLICE — SOURCE FAMILIES NOT YET TRIED:**

**(A) European national tech job boards** (these carry roles that never reach the ATS-domain searches):
- Poland (highest yield for English-speaking B2B contract work): NoFluffJobs, JustJoin.it, Bulldogjob, Pracuj.pl
- Germany/Austria: Softgarden-hosted boards, Honeypot, Xing, StepStone, Devjobs.at, Karriere.at, Gettyjobs
- France: Welcome to the Jungle (welcometothejungle.com), Talent.io
- Portugal/Spain: Landing.jobs, Tecnoempleo, Manfred (getmanfred.com)
- Netherlands/Belgium: Techgrounds, Magnet.me
- Nordics/Baltics: TheHub.io (DK/NO/SE), Jobbland, CVKeskus, CV.lv
- Czech/Slovak: Jobs.cz, StartupJobs.cz
- UK (FLAG these): Cord, Otta / Welcome to the Jungle UK, Hired
- Pan-Europe: EU Startups jobs, Sifted, Tech.eu, TechMeAbroad, Honeypot, Landing.jobs

**(B) Freelance / contract / fractional marketplaces and platforms.** He has a Partita IVA and contract is his normal working mode, but he has applied to ZERO of these. Check which are actually open to new talent right now and what the sign-up or application route is: **Malt** (very large in Italy and France — highest priority), A.Team, Braintrust, Toptal, Gun.io, Contra, Lemon.io, Twago, Freelancermap (DE), Comatch, Expert360, Andela, Turing, Gigster, Upwork Enterprise, Fiverr Pro, Worksome, YunoJuno (UK), Outvise, Talmix. For each, report: does it fit an EU-based Partita IVA contractor at ~3 years with an AI/automation profile, is it open or waitlisted, and what the concrete first step is. **NOTE: do NOT create accounts or sign up — just report the route and requirements.**

**(C) Italy-specific** (he lives there, so on-site is a PLUS and he'd be a local hire): InfoJobs.it, Monster.it, Codemotion Jobs, Wanted.it, Talent Garden, plus Milan/Rome/Bologna/Padua/Venice startup roles. English-working-language companies only, since his Italian is beginner.

Target titles: AI Engineer, AI Automation Engineer, Automation Consultant, Forward Deployed Engineer, Solutions Engineer, Implementation Engineer, Integration Engineer, Technical Consultant, RevOps Engineer, Internal Tools Engineer, Full-stack (TypeScript/Next.js/Laravel), Product Engineer, Technical Product Manager, QA Automation (Playwright).

ALREADY APPLIED OR SEEN — exclude: A-Players, Action1, Adaptyv, Akka, ALEA, Arize, Atmen, Atrix, Auditdata, Augment, Avenga, Avery, Axmed, BAS Group, Bob W, Camunda, Capco, CityZ, Clarasight, Cohere, DeepL, Duvo, Dwelly, EcoOnline, Edra, EggAI, ElevenLabs, Freeday, GLS/NXT, GTM Base, gravity9, Hexa, HiPeople, Hightouch, HICX, intent, Jamie, JetBrains, Laioutr, Lakera, LanguageWire, Lightning AI, Lleverage, Luma AI, Meticulous, Miaplaza, Mindspace, Mintos, Mistral, Moviris, n8n, Novosafe, Nuitée, OMMAX, Ophelos, Opply, Otherworldly, Outliant, Pigment, Pliant, Poolday, Postman, PubNub, Qdrant, Quadrivia, Re-Leased, Reasonable AI, Reedsy, Reflection, SERA, Spacelift, STRATOS, Scale AI, Seamflow, Shaman, Siena AI, Signicat, SolveAI, Space Inch, Spyrosoft, Starbridge, Super Technologies, SupportYourApp, Suspicious Antwerp, Taktile, Tangible, Teleport, TensorOps, The Flex, The Quality Group, VML, Vapi, WA.Technology, WTW, Zauber, Zensai, Zeotap, dexter health, nuwacom, opus, otonomee, indigo.ai, Claranet, epilot, chatarmin, it's prodigy, Bending Spoons, Satispay, Scalapay, Casavo, iGenius.

For each SURVIVOR: company | exact title | location wording VERBATIM | years or "none stated" | language req | salary if disclosed | employment or contract | posted date | CLEAN application URL | one honest sentence on fit | **form weight: CV-ONLY vs WRITTEN QUESTIONS** | VERIFIED_BY_FETCH or NEEDS_BROWSER.

Target 12-18 verified roles PLUS the marketplace report in (B). Say which boards were productive and which were dead.

Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- job-hunt: Find, verify and rank live job and contract openings that fit Prabhavit's CV — AI/automation engineering, forward-deployed and solutions engineering, full-stack product engineering, technical PM — remote-first from Italy but worldwide in scope, delivered as a ranked .xlsx shortlist. Use this skill whenever the conversation turns to looking for work — "find me some jobs", "any new roles this week", "who's hiring for X", "check openings at a named company", "any freelance or contract gigs going", "is this posting worth applying to" — or when asked to compare or re-rank roles already found. Trigger even when the request is vague ("anything interesting out there?"), names no job board, or mentions only a company or a technology rather than a role.
- morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

content.text: Both of my permitted tools are blocked. Let me confirm the exact state and check what an unblock path would look like.

Both permitted tools are hard-blocked. I could not verify a single role, and I'm not going to invent any. Here's the situation and what I can still give you.

## BLOCKER — the sweep could not run

**WebSearch: budget exhausted.** First call returned `this session has used its web search budget (200 of 200 WebSearch calls)`. Every subsequent call returns the same. Zero searches available.

**WebFetch: provenance-blocked.** Every call fails with `PROVENANCE_REQUIRED — web_fetch can only retrieve URLs that appeared in a user message, a prior web_fetch result, or an approved fetch prompt`. I tested six URLs including the two written as explicit domains in the brief (`welcometothejungle.com`, `getmanfred.com`) plus `thehub.io`, `landing.jobs`, NoFluffJobs and Malt. All six rejected. Because WebSearch is dead, nothing can seed the provenance set — and the brief's domains don't count, since a subagent task message isn't a user message. The two tools are deadlocked: WebFetch needed WebSearch to seed it, and WebSearch is gone.

I did not fall back to curl/python/bash, per your instruction.

**Roles verified: 0.** Boards productive: none. Boards dead: none — I never reached one, which is different from a board being dry and shouldn't be recorded as negative evidence. I have training data on job listings, but postings are ephemeral and reporting remembered ones as live would produce applications to roles that no longer exist. Not doing it.

**Unblock options, cheapest first:** (1) raise `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION` and re-run — restores both tools, since search reseeds fetch provenance; (2) paste 15-20 concrete board search URLs directly into a message to me, which seeds provenance and lets WebFetch alone carry the sweep; (3) a Chrome browser *is* connected (`Browser 1`, macOS, deviceId `6303e771-ab9f-4dec-a9d8-3417825f26ad`) — but browser use needs the user's own tool-selection consent and site permissions, and your brief scoped me to WebSearch/WebFetch, so I left it alone. Your call.

## (B) Marketplace report — FROM TRAINING DATA, NOT LIVE-VERIFIED

This is the one piece I can partly deliver, because signup routes change on a scale of years rather than days. **Every line below is unverified against the live site and my knowledge ends May 2026.** Treat as a triage order for a ~30-minute verification pass, not as fact. Open/waitlist status and fees are exactly the details that drift.

**Tier 1 — fits a Partita IVA holder at ~3 years, worth checking first**

- **Malt** — correctly your top pick. Huge in Italy and France, EU-native, built around exactly his situation: local freelancers with real legal status. Signup open, free; the gate is *profile validation*, not an interview, so a thin profile is the main failure mode. First step: build the profile at malt.it to 100% completion, set a day rate (~EUR 250-350 given his band), submit for validation. Note Comatch is now Malt Strategy — same company, but that arm is ex-consultant/senior and not his lane.
- **Lemon.io** — vetted, developer-specific, explicitly targets the 2-3+ year range rather than 8+. Screening call plus technical interview. Probably his single best odds-adjusted vetted network.
- **Freelancermap (DE)** — DACH B2B contract project board, open signup, exactly the contract mode he works in. Real caveat: a large share of listings require German, which is a hard gate for him. Worth checking the English-only subset.
- **Turing** — open signup, heavy automated vetting, and a lot of current volume is LLM/AI work that maps to his profile. Low effort to try.
- **Outvise** — Barcelona-based, EU-friendly, project-based, under-known so less crowded. Open application.

**Tier 2 — plausible but lower odds**

- **Braintrust** (open, free to talent, per-role screening, US-skewed roles), **Contra** (commission-free, open, but creative/marketing-skewed and lead quality is mixed), **Andela** (open application, global marketplace), **Twago** (Randstad-owned, EU, bidding model — bidding suits him poorly against low-cost competition), **Upwork** (note: "Enterprise" is a client-side product, not a talent tier — you get invited into it from a normal profile, so the first step is just a standard Upwork profile), **Fiverr Pro** (must build a Fiverr seller profile first, then apply to the Pro tier), **Worksome** (DK/UK, but volume is client-driven placement rather than self-serve browsing).

**Tier 3 — skip or deprioritise, with reasons**

- **A.Team, Gun.io, Gigster** — all pitched at senior/8+ year product builders. ~3 years is below the bar; applying burns time.
- **Toptal** — long multi-stage funnel (English interview, skill review, take-home project, live screen). Not impossible, but a poor time-to-outcome ratio versus Malt.
- **YunoJuno** — UK-centric, and he is not UK authorised. IR35 and UK payroll make most of it inaccessible. Flagging as you asked.
- **Comatch** — absorbed into Malt Strategy; ex-consultancy/senior profiles only. Not his lane.
- **Expert360** — Australian market. Geographically irrelevant.
- **Talmix** — business/consulting talent, minimal engineering. Weak fit.

No accounts created and no signups started, per your instruction — the above is route-and-requirements only.

## Recommendation

Re-run (A) and (C) once search budget is restored; those are genuinely untried source families and the reasoning behind picking them looks sound. Before acting on (B), spend ten minutes live-checking Tier 1 — Malt and Lemon.io especially, since those two carry most of the expected value and are the ones where a stale "signup is open" would waste real effort.
